bib.title: No Unbiased Estimator of the Variance of K-Fold Cross-Validation

question: Can the variance of the K-fold cross-validation estimate of generalization error be estimated without bias, and how much does ignoring test-error correlations underestimate it?
hypothesis: Naive variance estimators that ignore error correlations from overlapping training/test sets grossly underestimate the variance of K-fold CV.
contributions: Main theorem: no universal (valid under all distributions) unbiased estimator of the variance of K-fold cross-validation exists
Eigen-decomposition of the error covariance matrix: three eigenvalues, three variance components (sigma^2, omega, gamma)
Numerical experiments comparing the three components as problem difficulty and K vary

method.summary: Theory: by permutation symmetry the covariance of CV errors has three distinct values (sigma^2, omega, gamma), so Var[CV] = sigma^2/n + (m-1)/n omega + (n-m)/n gamma; any unbiased quadratic estimator would need an unsatisfiable linear system. Experiments estimate the three components by Monte Carlo from many independent training sets.
method.task: variance estimation of K-fold cross-validation / generalization error

datasets.name: Synthetic Gaussian regression (Exp 1 and 2)
datasets.size: n varied (training sample size on x axis of Fig 1, 4); d=30 inputs
datasets.split: Exp 2: K=10 folds, one sample of size n; Exp 1: K=10 independent train and test sets of size n
datasets.source: x ~ N(0,I) d=30; y = sqrt(3/d) sum x_k + eps, eps ~ N(0,1) (R2 about 3/4)
datasets.preprocessing: Outlier variant: x ~ N(0,I) with prob p=0.95, N(0,100I) otherwise; y = sqrt(3/(d(p+100(1-p)))) sum x_k + eps

datasets.name: Letter
datasets.split: treated as the population; independent training samples drawn by uniform sampling with replacement; K=10 folds
datasets.source: Letter data set (source not cited in text)
datasets.preprocessing: 26 classes collapsed to 2 classes (A to M) vs (N to Z)

models.name: Decision trees (Exp 3)
models.architecture: classification tree; pruning and settings not stated

inference.samples: Fig 1: variance of EPE estimated on 100,000 independent experiments; Exp 2 and 3: number of independent training samples used to estimate sigma^2, omega, gamma not stated (only 'many')

parameters.K: 10 in Exp 2 and 3; Fig 5 varies K at n=120

metrics.name: Contribution to Var[CV] of sigma^2, omega, gamma
metrics.definition: Var[CV]=theta = sigma^2/n + (m-1)/n omega + (n-m)/n gamma (Eq 7); sigma^2 = variance of a test error, omega = covariance within a test block, gamma = covariance between test blocks; shown as bar plots of each term's share

baselines: naive estimator theta1 ignoring correlations vs theta2 accounting for them (hold-out, Exp 1)
eval.protocol: Monte Carlo estimation of the moments from independent training sets; no significance tests; seeds not stated

availability.data: Letter dataset only; synthetic generator specified in text

evidence.quote: According to the number of training examples, σ2 is only responsible for 50 to 70 % of the total variance, so that a variance estimate based solely on σ2 has a negative bias of the order of magnitude of the variance itself.

results.claim: There exists no universally unbiased estimator of Var of K-fold cross-validation (Theorem 6): the constraints a=1/n, b=(m-1)/n, c=(n-m)/n, a+b+c=0 cannot hold together.
results.setup: Theory, any K, any distribution; quadratic estimators suffice by Lemmas 4 and 5; also holds for leave-one-out (K=n) and two-fold
results.note: Proof, not experiment. Reason: variance of the projection on the all-ones eigenvector (lambda3) cannot be estimated from one realization; repeating K-fold splits does not give independent realizations.

results.claim: On Letter (2-class, trees, K=10), the sigma^2 component alone is only 50 to 70% of the total variance of CV depending on training set size, so an estimator based only on sigma^2 is biased low by about the size of the variance.
results.metric: share of Var[CV] due to sigma^2 term
results.setup: Experiment 3, Letter data set (20,000 examples as population, 16 features, A-M vs N-Z), decision trees, K=10, independent training samples drawn with replacement; varied training size n (Fig 6)
results.quote: σ2 is only responsible for 50 to 70 % of the total variance
results.note: The percentage is the sigma^2 share (sigma^2/n) of the true total Var[CV]=theta, i.e. what an estimate counting only test-error variance would capture; the paper does not call it a 'naive within-fold estimate' and does not measure any specific naive estimator on Letter. Exact percentages per n are only in Fig 6 (not in text). Remainder is attributed mainly to gamma.

results.claim: With outliers in synthetic regression, omega has little effect but gamma's contribution is of the same order as sigma^2 even at a high examples-to-parameters ratio (up to 20).
results.setup: Experiment 2, OLS, d=30, K=10, outlier mixture p=0.95 (Fig 4)

results.claim: Without outliers, gamma matters at small sample sizes; at large n total variance falls and is mainly sigma^2.
No general trend of variance or its decomposition with K; minimum variance can be at K=n or at an intermediate K.
results.setup: Experiment 2, n=120, with and without outliers (Fig 5)

results.claim: In hold-out with independent train/test sets gamma=0 so an unbiased estimator exists (theta2); the correlation-ignoring theta1 is highly biased even for large n.
results.setup: Experiment 1, K=10 independent train/test sets, d=30, OLS, truth from 100,000 experiments (Fig 1)

limits: Only shows no estimator is unbiased for all distributions, not that none is useful; authors name building variance estimators for the dependence structure as the next step
Admissible (omega,gamma) region is very large so no estimator with universally small bias
Experiments are simple (linear model, trees, Letter reduced to 2 classes); numbers of Monte Carlo training sets for Exp 2 and 3, tree settings and exact per-n shares are not stated in text
Assumes symmetric algorithms and n a multiple of K; analysis does not cover repeated K-fold splits (not independent)

terms.definition: average variance of errors for true test examples when A is fed training sets of size m(K-1)
within-block covariance of test errors, from the common training set
between-blocks covariance due to dependence of training sets and test block Tk appearing in all Dl for l != k
